Project Engineer – Civil Infrastructure Western Sydney (near Western Sydney Airport) | Immediate Start
 Join a major civil infrastructure project helping deliver critical works within one of Australia's fastest-growing development corridors.
 ABOUT THE ROLE
 We are seeking an experienced Project Engineer to support the delivery of a large-scale civil infrastructure project involving bulk earthworks, utilities, roads, drainage and associated subdivision works.
 Working closely with the Project Manager and site delivery team, you will play a key role in coordinating subcontractors, managing consultant and design interfaces, resolving technical queries and ensuring works are delivered safely, efficiently and in accordance with project requirements.
 The role will involve significant coordination between site teams, subcontractors, design consultants and external stakeholders to ensure design documentation, approvals and construction activities remain aligned with the project programme.
 This is an excellent opportunity to join a growing contractor with a strong pipeline of work across Western Sydney.
 KEY RESPONSIBILITIES
 - Coordinate day-to-day project delivery activities across multiple work fronts.
 - Manage subcontractors, suppliers, consultants and design interfaces.
 - Coordinate with civil, structural, services and other design consultants to resolve technical and construction-related issues.
 - Manage subcontractor RFIs, technical queries and design clarifications, ensuring timely responses from relevant consultants.
 - Support design management activities, including design reviews, documentation coordination, constructability assessments and design changes.
 - Monitor design deliverables, approvals and outstanding information to ensure construction activities remain on programme.
 - Prepare and manage RFIs, NCRs, ITPs, SWMS reviews and project documentation.
 - Monitor programme, productivity and project milestones.
 - Assist with procurement, scope packages and subcontractor management.
 - Track project costs, variations and progress claims.
 - Support quality assurance and compliance activities across site.
 - Liaise with client representatives, authorities and key project stakeholders.
 - Prepare regular project reporting and progress updates.
 - Drive efficient project outcomes through proactive problem solving and coordination.
 SKILLS & EXPERIENCE
 - Experience as a Project Engineer within civil infrastructure, subdivisions or earthworks projects.
 - Strong understanding of bulk earthworks, roads, drainage and utility installation.
 - Demonstrated experience coordinating engineering consultants and managing design-related issues during construction.
 - Ability to manage subcontractor RFIs, technical queries and design documentation.
 - Experience reviewing construction drawings, identifying design discrepancies and coordinating practical solutions.
 - Strong subcontractor management, project documentation and stakeholder coordination skills.
 - Ability to manage competing priorities across multiple work fronts in a live construction environment.
 - Strong communication, organisational and problem-solving skills.
 - Proficient with project management and reporting systems such as Procore, Laminar or similar.
 - Relevant Civil Engineering qualification.
 THE OPPORTUNITY
 - Major infrastructure project within the Western Sydney Airport growth corridor.
 - Long-term project pipeline and strong job security.
 - Exposure to large-scale civil infrastructure and subdivision works.
 - Broad involvement across engineering, design coordination and construction delivery.
 - High-performing and collaborative project team.
 - Genuine career progression opportunities.
 THE DETAILS
 - Full-time, site-based position.
 - Western Sydney location.
 - Competitive salary package based on experience.
 - Immediate start available.
 HOW TO APPLY
 Apply now or contact us for a confidential discussion about the opportunity.

candidates.content_text:
ACCIONA is a global company, leading in the development of regenerative infrastructure that creates a positive impact on society. Our workforce consists of more than 65,000 professionals, present in more than 40 countries across the five continents, all contributing to our mission to design a better planet. Are you a passionate individual who wants to make a difference, promote sustainable development, and find solutions to the biggest global challenges, including climate change, overpopulation, and water scarcity? Come and join us in building the infrastructure our planet needs to achieve a sustainable future.
ACEREZ, a partnership of ACCIONA, COBRA and Endeavour Energy, has been appointed network operator by EnergyCo to design, build, finance, operate and maintain the Central-West Orana Renewable Energy Zone (REZ) transmission network. The ACCIONA COBRA Joint Venture (ACJV), the design and construct (D&C) consortium, will design and build the Central-West Orana REZ transmission project.
The Central-West Orana Renewable Energy Zone (REZ) Transmission Project will build new high-capacity transmission lines, energy hubs and supporting infrastructure to transfer power generated by solar and wind projects to electricity consumers. The new infrastructure is expected to be operational by 2028 and will initially unlock up to 4.5 gigawatts of new network capacity.
The project consists of 90km of 500kV overhead transmission lines and 150 km of 330kV transmission lines for generator connections, stretching from Elong Elong in the west through to Barigan Creek in the east, via an energy hub at Merotherie.
The Central-West Orana project is currently seeking a dedicated Site Engineer - Civil to share their expertise within our growing Energy Hubs and Substations Teams.
Key Responsibilities
- Ensure all quality and environmental aspects of the project are addressed to maintain effective operation and project delivery.
- Ensures non-conformances are recorded and corrective actions initiated as soon as practically possible.
- Completes all outstanding defects as required by the program.
- Prepares Inspection Test Reports and checklists that accurately reflect contract requirements.
- Provide support on planning the use of materials, resources, components or systems within the project, and construction practices and problems to ensure project success, value for money and best practice are achieved.
- Assist the Project Engineer with development of construction planning documents and monitor implementation.
- Maintain project schedule by monitoring project progress and coordinating activities.
- Assist with preparing project status reports and change orders.
- Assesses progress daily and prepares plan of works for daily cost planning meeting (if held)
- Responsible and accountable to ensure that the requirements of the Contract are being satisfied at work crew level.
- Coordinate resource allocation with the expectation that you would encourage effective teamwork and foster a positive attitude toward the achievement of organisational objectives.
- Tracks subcontractor resources daily and record accurately
- Prepares cost plan/resources for daily cost planning meeting.
Required Skills and Competencies
- Bachelor's degree (Engineering) Civil or Relevant Tertiary Education
- Experience constructing outdoor air insulated substations and substations at 220kV or above
- Tier 1 Contractor experience is preferred, on large scale projects
- Preferable 1 to 3 years post graduate experience in a construction / engineering environment
- Demonstrated ability to work effectively with others.
- Establish and steward overall delivery work plans.
- Ensuring all relevant regulatory requirements are satisfied.
- Competent in planning and organising work schedules.
- Working knowledge of HS&E requirements and implementation of same
- Clear communication - verbal and written
Site Engineer positions are bus in bus out, in camp style accommodation provided for 14 days onsite and 7 days off site, on a roster-based arrangement out of the Central West Orana Region, Merotherie.
This position is being delivered as part of a joint venture between two organisations. As such, your employment may be with either of the parent companies, and this will be confirmed during the recruitment process.
We welcome applicants of all backgrounds, identities, and experiences. If you believe you bring the capabilities to succeed in this role, we'd love to hear from you. We look forward to continuing to build our supportive workplace together.
For more information on how your personal data is managed, please refer to the privacy statements of each parent company:
Grupo Cobra: https://www.grupocobra.com/en/privacy-policy/

Site / Project Engineer - Civil & Concrete
Oakleigh Civil - South Australia
Join a growing South Australian civil construction company and build your career across project engineering, construction delivery, estimating and commercial management. 
About Oakleigh Civil 
Oakleigh Civil is a South Australian civil construction company specialising in civil infrastructure and structural concrete projects. Our capabilities include formwork, reinforcement, concrete placement and excavation. 
We work with on major infrastructure projects across metropolitan and regional South Australia, as well as interstate. 
Our work spans water infrastructure, defence, renewable energy, roads, mining and electrical infrastructure. 
Our experienced team takes a practical approach to delivering projects safely and to a very high standard. We value strong client relationships and take pride in being a contractor our clients can rely on.
About the role 
We are seeking a motivated Site / Project Engineer with at least three years’ construction experience to join our growing team. 
Working closely with the Construction Manager, company management, site supervisors and clients, you will help plan, coordinate and deliver projects from tender stage through to completion.  
The role combines site-based project management, estimating and commercial responsibilities. Unlike a traditional site engineering role, you will have exposure to the full project lifecycle, including estimating, procurement, construction delivery, cost control, variations, progress claims and project close-out. 
The successful candidate will be expected to take ownership of assigned projects, identify issues early and work with the project team to develop practical solutions. 
This position suits someone who is looking to broaden their capabilities, take greater responsibility and develop their career within a growing civil construction business.
Key responsibilities 
- Plan and coordinate construction activities with site supervisors to meet project requirements and construction programs. 
- Take ownership of allocated projects from planning through to completion. 
- Maintain regular communication with clients regarding project progress, upcoming works and any issues requiring resolution. 
- Review drawings, specifications and scope documents, identify issues, discrepancies, risks and constructability issues. 
- Assist with estimating, quantity take-offs, quotations and tender submissions. 
- Prepare and maintain project schedules, budgets, forecasts and progress reports. 
- Monitor project costs, cost-to-complete and forecasts. 
- Prepare and track project costs, variations and progress claims. 
- Coordinate procurement of materials, subcontractors and suppliers in accordance with project requirements and programs. 
- Coordinate project quality requirements, including ITP’s, inspections, testing, NCR’s and handover documentation. 
- Maintain accurate project documentation, registers, correspondence and records. 
- Support site safety requirements and work with supervisors to ensure works are planned and delivered safely. 
- Provide practical engineering and constructability advice to site teams. 
- Build and maintain effective relationships with clients, contractors and suppliers. 
About you 
- A degree in Civil Engineering or a relevant engineering discipline. 
- At least three years’ experience as a Site or Project Engineer in construction. 
- Experience in civil infrastructure or structural concrete works; formwork, reinforcement and concrete placement experience will be highly regarded. 
- Ability to interpret construction drawings, specifications and technical requirements. 
- Understanding of construction programming, project cost control, quality assurance and WHS requirements. 
- Strong organisation, communication and problem-solving skills. 
- Experience with variations, progress claims and project documentation. 
- Ability to manage competing priorities across multiple projects. 
- A practical approach, initiative and willingness to work closely with site supervisors and site crews. 
- Ability to identify problems early and take ownership of finding practical solutions. 
- Willingness and ability to work away from home when required. 
- A genuine desire to develop your skills and progress your career within a growing construction business. 
Why Join Oakleigh Civil?
- Varied projects: Work on civil infrastructure and structural concrete projects in metropolitan and regional South Australia, as well as interstate. 
- Broader experience: Gain exposure to the full project lifecycle, including estimating, procurement, construction, commercial management and project close out. 
- Direct involvement: Work closely with Construction Manager, company management and experienced site teams with the opportunity to influence how projects are delivered. 
- Career development: Build your capabilities across project management, estimating and commercial management, with genuine pathway to increase responsibility as the company grows. 
- Make a Contribution: Bring your ideas and help improve the way we work that supports Oakleigh Civil’s continued growth. 
Apply now 
If you’re looking to take the next step in your engineering career with Oakleigh Civil, apply through SEEK with your CV and a brief cover letter outlining your relevant experience.

bullets: Work from home opportunities
Genuine work-life balance and flexible working arrangements
Employee wellness program and a range of lifestyle benefits
candidates.content_text:
Division: Planning & Place
Business Unit: Strategic & Place Planning
Title: Graduate Urban Designer, Permanent - Full-time Role, 35 hours per week
Salary Range: $77,285.31 to $89,818.38 per annum + super (subject to skills and experience)
Who we are:
Stretching from Palm Beach to Manly, the Northern Beaches boasts more than half of all the beaches in Sydney and a population of more than 270,000. Northern Beaches Council strives to deliver the highest quality services to our community. We are proud to be the winner of the Bluett Award 2022 and the 2022 Change Champion Award in the Enterprise Category. Join us and you’ll be part of an organisation committed to promoting sustainable growth, leading the community, protecting our environment, and creating a great future for the Northern Beaches.
Strategic and Place Planning:
Strategic and Place Planning prepares sustainable land use and design strategies, policies and plans for Council’s diverse range of localities, including established urban areas, urban renewal activity centres, future growth areas, employment areas, rural lands, and environmentally significant areas.
The Strategic and Place Planning Business Unit delivers the following services:
• Strategic Land-Use Planning and Planning Proposal assessment
• Land Use Policy Development
• Urban Land Release
• Heritage and Structure Planning
• Urban Design and Place Planning
• Infrastructure Contributions Planning and administration
Key projects our team is currently working on include Place Plan preparation, a Structure Plan for Brookvale, preparation of new comprehensive Local Environmental Plan and Development Control Plan, referral assessments for the Frenchs Forest Precinct, a Thematic Heritage Study, and a review of Council’s Affordable Housing Policy.
Northern Beaches Council is committed to safeguarding children and young people. Council acknowledges that protecting the safety of children and young people is a whole of community responsibility and is everyone’s business.
Working with us:
Northern Beaches Council provides a comprehensive range of benefits focused on our employees’ lifestyle, health and wellbeing, recognition and career development. In this role you’ll enjoy -
• Work from home opportunities
• Genuine work-life balance and flexible working arrangements
• Employee wellness program and a range of lifestyle benefits
• High level of technological innovation and systems
• Values based culture and a teams-orientated working environment
Our opportunity:
Reporting to the Manager, Strategic & Place Planning and under the guidance of the Principal Urban Designer, the Graduate Urban Designer supports the delivery of Council's urban design, place planning and strategic planning program while developing professional knowledge and practical experience across a broad range of urban design disciplines.
The role provides an opportunity for an emerging urban design professional to build technical capability through involvement in strategic planning, development assessment, place planning and public domain projects. Working alongside experienced practitioners, the Graduate Urban Designer contributes to high-quality design outcomes while participating in a structured program of mentoring and professional development.
The position supports the delivery of Council's Urban Design work program and contributes to creating sustainable, liveable and well-designed places across the Northern Beaches.
Additional Information:
Position Description
Applications close on: Friday 6 November 2026
Expected Interview Date: Thursday 10 December 2026
Questions? Please call the Hiring Manager: Phil Jemison (02) 8495 6262
Northern Beaches Council is a diverse and inclusive employer and encourages applications from differently abled candidates. Reasonable adjustments to the workplace may be made where these are required.
If you would like to contact us to discuss your specific circumstances, please contact the hiring manager for this role. If you do not feel comfortable to do so, please contact HR Services on (02) 8495 5070.

candidates.title: Undergraduate Engineer
candidates.abstract: A rare opportunity to join a business that has been in operation for 90+ years and is focused on creating, connecting and caring for communities.
bullets: Tier 1 Construction & Utilities contractor
Make a real impact and engage in meaningful work
Be rewarded & recognised for the 'Good Work' you do!
candidates.content_text:
Life at Fulton Hogan is about making the most of opportunities, taking responsibility, and making it happen. We appreciate our peoples' courage, curiosity and unique perspectives, and look to collaborate as much as possible to explore safer, smarter and more efficient ways of working in this rapidly changing world. We don't stand still - there are always opportunities to do more and do better.
- Keen to progress your career? Take full advantage of our tailored training, leadership, and mentoring programs; or leverage our partnerships with industry association such as Engineers Australia, the Australian Water Association, WaterAid, Chartered Accountants, CPA Australia, Infrastructure Sustainability Council, The National Association of Women in Construction, plus many more.
- Looking to enhance your wellbeing? We will encourage you to explore flexible working arrangements where possible. We offer great benefits, including corporate health and fitness programs, health insurance discounts, personal banking support, a range of retailer discounts, up to 18 weeks paid primary carers parental leave and up to 10 days paid secondary carers leave, access to our Employee Assistance Program (including your immediate family), and the option to take more time for yourself throughout the year with our Purchase Leave Policy.
- Want to help us better the communities we live and work in? Our purpose of creating, connecting, and caring for communities is more than a saying to us - it's a way of thinking, working, and living because we're locals too, and seek to give back in ways that strengthen and build resilient communities. We do this because we genuinely care, enjoy what we do, and even manage to have some fun along the way! You'll find us partnering with local and national community groups, like Clontarf Foundation, and Black Dog Institute, in addition to indigenous groups and social enterprises, to ensure that our good work positively impacts and brings about sustainable change within our industry.
- Do we offer a 'competitive' salary package? Of course! Speak to our Talent Acquisition or People & Culture team to learn more.
What's on offer?
We are seeking a highly energetic and motivated Undergraduate Engineer to join our Fulton Hogan Utilities business in Victoria. This is a fantastic opportunity for you to gain practical, industry experience while building your engineering career. You'll receive on-the-job learning, coaching and support from experienced professionals, along with access to excellent employee benefits and future career pathways.
This is a casual position with an initial 12-week commitment, with the opportunity to continue and progress for the right candidate. Following graduation, there may also be an opportunity to transition into the Fulton Hogan Graduate Program.
This isn't a role where you'll be sitting on the sidelines. From day one, you'll be involved in infrastructure projects, working alongside our site teams to help plan, coordinate and deliver construction activities.
You'll gain exposure to the key elements of project delivery, including safety, quality, environment, cost, programme and community outcomes, and develop an understanding of how they all come together in practice.
About you
- Current Undergraduate student pursuing a qualification in Civil or Mechanical Engineering
- A practical, hands-on approach and strong problem-solving skills
- A genuine commitment to safety
- Strong communication and teamwork skills
- Curiosity, resilience and a willingness to learn
- Flexibility to travel and work occasional weekends or night shifts when required
- Alignment with our values: Respect, Energy & Effort, Attitude and Leadership
- Commitment to Fulton Hogan's Fulton Hogan's Living Safely 2.0 Culture.
Eligibility
- To be eligible, you must:
- Have valid working rights in Australia
- Hold a current driver's license and have access to a reliable vehicle
- Be currently completing a relevant undergraduate degree and be in your third or fourth year of study
- Hold, or be willing to obtain, a Construction White Card.
Our people share the same set of values that keep us REAL. Respect, Energy and Effort, Attitude and Leadership encapsulate what we stand for at Fulton Hogan and encourage us to foster a diverse and inclusive culture where we listen to, care for, celebrate, and respect everyone.
We are committed to reconciliation and building and nurturing respectful relationships with First Nations peoples. Through our First Nations Engagement Strategy and Reconciliation Action Plan (RAP), we aim to promote opportunities, cultural understanding and partnerships that celebrate and acknowledge the contributions of Indigenous communities.
If our values resonate with you, please submit an application for the position.
For over 90 years, Fulton Hogan has been delivering high-quality infrastructure to improve the lives of people every day. Our 10,000+ team works in every kind of weather and environment, creating, connecting, and caring for communities across Australia, New Zealand and the South Pacific.

candidates.title: Geotechnical/Tailings Engineer – Perth, Western Australia
candidates.abstract: Build your technical and consulting skills in this hands-on geotechnical role working across mining, tailings & infrastructure projects.
bullets: Gain hands-on experience from site investigations to analysis & reporting
Work across mining, tailings & infrastructure projects in WA and beyond
Full time role: Level 1/235 St Georges Terrace, Perth
candidates.content_text:
- Work on geotechnical projects across mining, tailings, and infrastructure
- Gain hands-on experience in site investigations, analysis, and reporting
- Full time role: Tetra Tech Coffey, Level 1/235 St Georges Terrace, Perth
- Salary range of A$ 88,500 to A$ 90,000 inclusive of superannuation
The Role
At Tetra Tech Coffey, we work on complex geotechnical challenges, delivering solutions across mining, tailings, and infrastructure projects. In this role, you’ll be involved in the full project lifecycle, from site investigations to geotechnical analysis and reporting.
You’ll work on projects that include tailings storage facilities, mine site geotechnics, earthworks, and slope stability, developing both technical and consulting skills. You’ll also have opportunities to engage directly with clients and stakeholders, gaining experience in project management and technical delivery.
This full-time role provides exposure to both fieldwork and office-based assessments, working closely with senior geotechnical engineers on projects throughout Western Australia and beyond. 
You’ll be part of a strong national geotechnical team while working within a supportive and growing Perth office.
About You
We’re looking for someone eager to apply technical knowledge in a consulting environment, with strong communication skills and a proactive approach to learning.
You’ll bring:
- A degree in Civil Engineering or Geotechnical Engineering
- A minimum of 12 months experience with tailings storage facilities
- An understanding of soil and rock logging, in situ testing, and monitoring instruments
- Exposure to mine site geotechnics, earthworks, and slope stabilization
- A willingness to travel to mine sites and remote project locations
- An interest in developing management, business development, and analytical skills
This is an opportunity to grow your career in mining and geotechnical engineering, gain diverse experience, and work alongside industry leaders. If you're ready to take the next step, we’d love to hear from you.
Why Tetra Tech Coffey?
- You’re keen to be involved in a mix of high-profile Australian and international projects across multiple sectors and are excited by the potential to travel to remote places.
- You enjoy working on unique and interesting projects and want to be a part of developing leading approaches to environmental assessment.
- You want to be part of a diverse and inclusive team that has a small company feel and large company opportunities.
- You want to work in a workplace that is supportive and encouraging, and there is always someone willing to help.
The Perks:
- Work-Life Balance: Flexible work options, study breaks, and the ability to buy extra leave - up to 8 weeks per year!
- Diverse Projects: Work across a wide variety of projects, clients, and sectors.
- Growth Opportunities: Professional development, coaching, and mentorship from our top experts.
- Memberships: Professional memberships to help you stay ahead in your field.
- Ownership: Participate in our employee stock purchase plan.
- Parental Leave: Paid leave for both primary and secondary caregivers.
- Support: Employee assistance program for you and your immediate family.
- Travel Discounts: Great deals through our corporate traveller program.
- Car Leasing: Take advantage of novated vehicle leasing options.
About Us 
Tetra Tech Coffey provides high-end environmental, geotechnical, digital, and engineering design consulting services. 
Every day, our people come together to solve complex challenges for our clients. 
With over 30,000 Tetra Tech colleagues across 550 offices globally, we deliver projects that improve lives through science, technology, and innovation. Our commitment to creating lasting, measurable value is reflected in our global 1 Billion People Challenge, which tracks how our 100,000+ annual projects benefit people and communities around the world.

candidates.title: Draftsperson - Modular Construction
candidates.abstract: Start your estimating career with hands-on experience in one of WA’s leading residential building companies.
bullets: Be valued for your innovation and curiosity
Genuine opportunities for career growth and progression
Permanent | Fulltime | Based in Canning Vale
candidates.content_text:
About the role
Summit Homes Group is looking for an enthusiastic and detail-oriented Trainee Estimator to join our Modular team in Canning Vale.
This is a great opportunity to start your career in residential construction, learning how building costs are calculated, materials are priced and estimates are prepared to support the construction of our modular homes.
Working alongside our experienced Estimating team, you'll receive hands-on training and support as you develop your skills and confidence. As your knowledge grows, you'll gradually take on more responsibility and work towards preparing estimates independently.
Some of the things you'll learn and be involved in include:
- Assisting with preparing cost estimates for new homes, contracts and building variations.
- Learning to read building plans and calculate material quantities and costs.
- Checking supplier pricing, maintaining accurate records and reviewing cost information.
- Working with our Sales, Drafting and Construction teams to support projects.
You'll also gain experience using estimating software and develop a practical understanding of building materials, construction processes and industry requirements.
About you 
We're looking for someone who enjoys working with numbers, has an eye for detail and is keen to learn something new.
You don't need previous construction or estimating experience – we'll provide the training and support to help you succeed.
You might be starting your career, have experience in administration or customer service, or simply be looking for a new direction.
What we're looking for:
- Good numerical skills and attention to detail.
- Confidence using computers, particularly Microsoft Excel.
- Strong organisational and communication skills.
- A positive attitude, willingness to learn and ability to work as part of a team.
Most importantly, we're looking for someone who is reliable, curious and ready to build their skills in a supportive environment.
If this sounds like an opportunity you'd enjoy, we'd love to hear from you.
What we offer 
- Permanent position
- Flexible working hours
- Free parking on site
- Competitive salary
- Corporate. company and supplier discounts
- Wellness programs
- Rewards and Recognition programs
- Ongoing training and development
- Industry leading culture
 Who we are 
Summit Homes Group is one of Western Australia's leading construction, property, and finance companies. Founded in 1978, Summit has helped over 45,000 West Australians realise their new home dreams over 48 years. Our core philosophy, Built Around People, ensures our dedicated and passionate staff have a great experience at work, which translates into exceptional building journeys for our customers. We know our people are our greatest strength, and their talent and commitment have been recognised with back-to-back HIA Professional Major Builder awards (2020-2025), underscoring Summit's industry leadership, quality, and dedication to excellence. With over 18 brands and 800 employees across our Group, we are always looking for team members who embody our company values and are enthusiastic about making a real difference to our business.
 Where you'll be working 
You’ll be based at our Summit Modular facility in Canning Vale, working alongside our production and construction team to manufacture and assemble quality modular homes.
You’ll be part of Summit Homes Group, one of WA’s established residential building groups, while working within an innovative and growing area of residential construction.
 Applications close on 10th November 2026 (Summit Homes group reserves the right to remove advertised roles before this date)
 We accept that everyone is unique. We believe that our differences make us stronger, and our success is enhanced by the diversity within our teams. We encourage applications from First Nations people, those identifying as LGBTQIA+, females, people of all ages, with disabilities and culturally and linguistically diverse people.

candidates.abstract: QLD Government department to delivering road infrastructure projects. Multiple contract roles available in Preservation & Maintenance team.
candidates.content_text:
Civil Engineers - Road Infrastructure & Maintenance
- Gold Coast, QLD
- Initial contracts through to October 2027
- Flexible working arrangement
About the Role
We are partnering with a large Queensland Government department to recruit multiple Engineers across various seniority levels (PO3 - PO5) to join the Preservation & Maintenance team. The team is responsible for maintaining and protecting infrastructure assets while enhancing and improving safety through delivery of maintenance, rehabilitation and various safety projects.
PO5 Principal Engineer - RPEQ Mandatory
- Provide reports on the progress of works and actual and forecast expenditure.
- Act as "Representative of the Principal" for the delivery of contracts as defined and delegated at respective project phases.
- Ensure all quality and environmental aspects of the project are identified and addressed to maintain effective operation and project delivery.
- Manage the calling and assessment of tenders and the contract awarding process for construction projects in the Region's Roads Implementation Program.
- Provide high level engineering advice and input into planning and design suitability and options, the use of materials, resources, components or systems within the project, and construction practices and problems to ensure project success, value for money and best practice are achieved.
- The role is also required to assist graduates, other engineers and technical staff to resolve technical issues on projects and mentor them to deliver programs on time and to budget.
PO4 Senior Engineer - RPEQ Mandatory
- Act as a Project Manager, as well as Contract Administrator to ensure that quality and value for money for the department has been achieved. The position will need the ability to quickly acquire knowledge and understanding of policies and legislation for engagement of consultants and contractors, and the forms of contract used for this purposes.
- Manage, assist, deliver and co-ordinate the delivery of Pre-construction activities to the region on time and to budget. This includes managing preliminary investigations such as survey and geotechnical, all land resumption requirements, all design tender actions and manage concept design through to detail design and the tender process.
- Assist graduates, other engineers, and technical staff to resolve technical issues on their projects and mentor them to deliver programs on time and to budget.
- Provide agreed customer service by attending to all public enquiries (which requires technical input) through appropriate channel and in a timely manner.
- Assess construction tenders and manage procurement phase
PO3 Engineer 
- Under supervision, project manage the delivery of road infrastructure projects through the administration of contracts and provision of technical expertise and support to the design, construction, and maintenance processes. 
- Determine appropriate bridge and road maintenance procedures, work instructions and manage road and bridge maintenance tasks.
- Assist in the selection of the most suitable contract process for project delivery, then administer the contract to ensure compliance and successful delivery
- Calculate quantities of component materials, analyse test results for materials, identify non-conformances, determine the controls needed during construction, and conduct and manage risk assessment
About You
- Experience in civil infrastructure, road construction, maintenance or rehabilitation.
- Strong project management, contract administration and stakeholder engagement skills.
- Bachelor of Engineering 
- Valid Drivers licence 
To Apply
If you meet the mandatory requirements and are ready to contribute to major regional infrastructure, submit your resume and cover letter detailing your relevant experience today. Contact Clarissa Anderson - 0475 900 876 or clarissa.anderson@randstad.com.au

Earn while you learn
Experience a variety of career pathways
candidates.content_text:
Building for Generations through the Pursuit of Excellence
The FKG Construction team has a proud 50+ year history of successfully delivering a variety of commercial construction projects across a wide range of sectors including both government and private clients. We are dedicated to building for generations, achieved through our personable approach with all people, including those within our communities within which we live every day.
We believe our people are the key to our success and we are invested in supporting the wellbeing of our team members, providing skills development opportunities, rewarding performance and recognising high achievement.
As an FKG Group employee you will have access to our range of benefits which includes corporate health insurance discounts, employee assistance program, our “Thrive” wellbeing initiative and many more.
The Role
Keen to kick start your career in the construction industry and work alongside your degree? Then look no further!  Due to recent organisational growth we are looking for our next superstar Cadet!
A cadetship at FKG will give you knowledge across all areas of construction, you'll learn from experienced members of the team, obtain hands-on involvement across a variety of exciting commercial projects and be given excellent learning support and mentorship as you develop your career.
Responsibilities
You will enjoy the variety within your job scope, including:
- Organisation and management of suppliers and subcontractors
- Procurement of trade packages and assistance in developing cost reports;
- Liaison with clients, site staff, design managers, estimators, and project managers
- Estimation, design and contract administration
Experience and Qualifications
 To be considered for this role, you will need:
- To be currently enrolled and successfully completed the first year of your Bachelor of Construction Management/ Urban Development/ Quantity Surveying
- Highly developed organisational, time management and prioritising skills A can-do attitude, self-motivated and willingness to learn;
- An exceptional level of verbal and written communication and interpersonal skills Previous construction industry experience would be an advantage;
- To include your ATAR results on your resume.
Apply Now!
- FKG is an equal opportunity employer, where we recognise the diversity of our team and actively promote equality of opportunity for all with the right mix of talent, skills and potential. We welcome all applications from a wide range of candidates. Selection for roles will be based on individual merit alone. 
- Apply with “Quick Apply” or email hr@fkg.com.au with your CV.

candidates.abstract: Crucial role in the continued success of UGL Regional Linx safely operating and maintaining the Country Regional Network in regional NSW
candidates.location: Bathurst, Blue Mountains & Central West NSW
bullets: Historic piece of regional NSW rail infrastructure
Excellent long term career prospects
Work in a motivated, inclusive, high performing and flexible environment
candidates.content_text:
About UGL Regional Linx
At UGL Regional Linx (UGLRL), we help connect communities across regional New South Wales by managing and maintaining the Country Regional Network (CRN). As a subsidiary of UGL Transport, we are proud to create meaningful employment opportunities in regional and rural communities, with more than 85% of our workforce based across regional NSW.
We are committed to creating an inclusive workplace where people feel valued, supported, and empowered to succeed. Guided by our core values, we foster a culture built on collaboration, respect, safety, innovation, and continuous improvement.
Job Purpose
The Estimator is responsible for preparing project estimates with accurate cost allocations and up to date market knowledge, monitoring the performance of project estimates, managing the change control process associated with project estimates, maintaining the CATS Resource Library with current benchmarked rates, and leading the overall 3MWP estimation process with the support of Infrastructure delivery team subject matter experts, the Procurement team, Finance team, and Assets & Engineering subject matter experts. 
The Estimator supports Project Owners by preparing and updating cost estimates for variations and facilitating the conversion of provisional sums to fixed-cost submissions.
What You'll Be Doing
Be responsible for the estimation of the 3 Year Maintenance Works Program, including the supervision and management of external and internal resources used during the process of estimation
Prepare detailed estimates for every project in the 3MWP in line with the Project Controls Plan process for estimation.
Assist in the preparation of UGLRL Enhancements estimates as required, including the loading of those estimates into CATS
Preparing and updating Estimates for Variations and conversion of Provisional Sum to Fixed Costs submissions
Maintain the UGL Regional Linx CATS Register and Master Resource Library
Maintain up to date Labour, Plant, Material rates within the Master Resource Library
Develop and maintain an “Estimating Manual” for UGLRL Projects. 
Review all project documentation to understand the requirements of the work to include the analysis of technical, contractual and financial requirements.
Explore opportunities for innovation while identifying risk and opportunities.
Maintain accurate and details estimate files.
Maintain awareness of best practice in the industry
Develop innovative estimates and options through knowledge of the latest design and or construction techniques to deliver the best possible outcome for UGLRL
Coordinates and collaborates with subject matter experts on methodology, program, IR, Plant and estimate review processes
Perform trend analysis and actively evaluate project cost and estimate performance
About You
Tertiary qualification in Engineering, Quantity Surveying or similar profession. (Desirable)
3+ years’ experience working in an estimating role
Knowledge of construction, material components, regulations and estimating
Sound knowledge and experience within the rail industry, especially in an O&M context
Ability to read and interpret drawings/plans and specifications
Why Join UGL Regional Linx?
Be part of an organisation that plays a vital role in connecting regional communities.
Work within a supportive and collaborative team environment.
Access opportunities for professional growth and career development.
Contribute to projects with lasting community and infrastructure impact.
Join a business that values diversity, inclusion, and different perspectives.
Diversity & Inclusion
At UGL Regional Linx, we believe diverse teams create better outcomes. We welcome applications from people of all backgrounds, experiences, and identities.
We are particularly committed to increasing female representation across our business and strongly encourage women to apply, even if you don't meet every requirement listed.
We also encourage applications from Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples, people living with disability, culturally and linguistically diverse candidates, LGBTQIA+ individuals, and mature-age professionals.
Our recruitment process may include national criminal history checks and pre-employment medical assessments, including drug and alcohol screening.
